newsitem.title: USA: CSCE coffee called to open up 5.00 to 8.00 cents.
newsitem.headline: CSCE coffee called to open up 5.00 to 8.00 cents.

text.p: CSCE coffee futures were called to open up 5.00 to 8.00 cents Friday, although many traders said the market was likely to come in closer to unchanged.

"It's called 5.00 to 8.00 higher on numbers," said one trader. "But I think it will be half that. People are waiting for the USDA numbers and unless some other fundamental news comes out, I doubt we'll make 8.00 higher."
USDA's world coffee production estimates are slated for release after today's close. The report was expected to include USDA's first forecast for top-grower Brazil's 1997/98 harvest.
Early estimates from industry participants in Brazil have put next season's crop at anywhere from 20 million to 25 million 60-kg bags, compared with this year's yield of at least 27 million.

Most U.S.-based traders said they expected the USDA figure for 1997/98 to surpass the Brazil trade forecasts. Sources said former USDA coffee agronomist Leon Yallouz put the 1997/98 Brazil crop at 27.5 million bags, but the figure has not been confirmed.

Thursday, New York arabica futures ended mostly firmer in a consolidation. Active September ended up 2.30 cents at 192.40 cents a lb, well below the session high of 198 cents. July finished 0.15 firmer at 207.80, having traded from 204.50 to 217.50.
The July/September switch narrowed to 15.40 cents at the close, from 17.55 on Wednesday.
On the charts, September would need to clear 199.50 to 200.00 cents to solidify its stance, while scale-down trade buying was expected to emerge toward the 190-cent mark.
After Thursday's close, CSCE said certified coffee stocks fell by 46 60-kg bags as of June 11, to 44,784 bags. There were 5,500 bags pending grading, the exchange said.
London robusta futures were firmer but off the highs by Friday's midday break, with LIFFE July up $35 to $1,800 and September $40 higher, at $1,835.
